name: Camp Modin
operator_name: KEF Camping Co. Inc. dba Camp Modin
description_short: A co-ed Jewish overnight camp on Salmon Lake in Maine's Belgrade Lakes region, for ages 7-16. It offers 3.5-week and 7-week sessions covering land and water sports, arts, performing arts and wilderness trips, with Shabbat observance and a kosher kitchen.
special_needs_notes: Diet only: kosher kitchen, with vegetarian and gluten-free options. The camp says it is nut and sesame aware and can handle certain food allergies, with details on request. The page does not mention support for other special needs.
swim_waterfront_notes: On Salmon Lake, which the camp describes as a clear, sand-bottom, spring-fed lake with water around 75-80°F. Activities include swim lessons, general swim, sailing, canoeing and water-skiing with four tournament ski boats.

sources.note: Drafted by the listing tool from this page

source.title: Parents: Everything You Need to Know: Camp Modin, Belgrade, Maine

warnings: The rates table is headed "Summer 2026", but every session date in it is in 2027. The weekdays given (for example Wed. June 23) match the 2027 calendar, so I recorded this as the 2027 season. Ask the camp to confirm the rates are for 2027.
Prices shown are the discounted rates for cash, ACH or wire payments. Paying by credit card costs 3% more.
The only mailing address on the page is incomplete ("Suite 265H, Scarsdale, NY 10583"). It looks like the office address, not the camp's location in Belgrade, Maine.

Optional extras cost more: linen service $380 per session, horseback riding $595, golf $575, the Yonkers bus $260 each way, the Portland shuttle $95 each way and the Boston Logan shuttle $160 each way. There are also grade-specific trip fees.
The page gives drive times that don't match: Boston is "three hours" in one place and "roughly two hours" in another, and New York City is six hours in one place and five in another.
The page doesn't say whether the 3.5-week sessions are open to every age.
